product: Reserve power: TPPL lead-acid and a new lithium battery for data centers, telecom/broadband (DOCSIS 4.0) and utility substations (SEC 8-K 2026-08-12; Investor Day transcript 2026-06-11). Precision Power: defense/aerospace lithium for soldier power, drones and standoff weapons. Industrial Mobility: forklift batteries and Class 8 APUs (Jefferies transcript, aggregator).
demand: Price-led. Q1 FY27 growth was +3% pricing, +1% FX, +1% organic volume (SEC 8-K 2026-08-12). FY26 was +3% price, +2% FX, +1% acquisitions, -2% organic volume (SEC 8-K 2026-05-20). Mix is favourable: NIS +9.4% and PPS +23.6% offset IMS -3.2%.
pricing_power: Loss or phase-out of IRC 45X credits, which added $47.2M, 5.0 points, to Q1 FY27 gross profit and lift GM to 33.5% from 28.5% ex-45X (SEC 8-K 2026-08-12). Also the non-recurring $30.9M tariff refunds, a deeper IMS recession, lithium cell cost inflation, Tijuana closure charges and adverse FX.
competition: Yes. Chinese LFP and lithium cells are the cheap substitute and are available commercially now; the CEO says China controls about 99% of the LFP material and supply chain (2026-06-11 Investor Day, aggregator). They are not FEOC-compliant for US defense programs, so EnerSys's domestic alternative only arrives when Greenville, about 1 GWh, starts construction in H1 FY2028 (SEC 8-K 2026-07-23).
market_strategy: At Investor Day on 2026-06-11 CEO Shawn O'Connell and CFO Andi Funk promised a long-term framework: 4-8% annual revenue growth, 3-5% end-market growth and 50-100 bps margin expansion per year, aided by about $875M of remaining buyback (transcript, aggregator). On 2026-08-12 O'Connell pledged a dividend growing with earnings excluding 45X (SEC 8-K).
bull: Q1 FY27 sales $935.6M +4.8% and adj EPS $3.66 beat $2.83 consensus; dividend +10%; net leverage 0.8x; data-center revenue ~$500M FY27 with lead-acid orders up mid-80s y/y (SEC 8-K 2026-08-12).
bear: EPS leaned on $47.2M 45X credit plus $30.9M tariff refunds; ex both $1.78. IMS fell 3.2% y/y, growth was price-led, and Chinese LFP is a cheap substitute until Greenville starts H1 FY2028.
falsifier: Q2 FY27 adjusted EPS ex-45X below $1.95 or sales below $955M, reported about early November 2026 (SEC 8-K 2026-08-12 guidance).
sources: https://x.com/EnerSys (read, parked OKK account, not the company)
web_what_changed_30_90d: In 90 days: 2026-07-23 EnerSys refined the Greenville SC lithium plant to defense focus, ~$500M net investment, revised ~$150M DOE grant (SEC 8-K). 2026-08-12 Q1 FY27 sales $935.6M +4.8% and adj EPS $3.66 +64%, plus a 10% dividend raise to $0.2875 (SEC 8-K). Last 30 days quiet: only Roth MKM reiterated Buy $265 on 2026-09-24 (stockanalysis, aggregator).
web_true_now_not_modelled: Q1 FY27 adj EPS $3.66 leaned on a $47.2M IRC 45X credit plus $30.9M one-time tariff refunds; ex both it was $1.78, +42% (SEC 8-K 2026-08-12). Net leverage fell to 0.8x, cash $530.7M. Lithium data-center product launched summer 2026, in validation; data-center revenue ~$500M FY27 with lead-acid orders up mid-80s y/y (Jefferies transcript ~2026-09-12, aggregator).
web_demand_product: Reserve power: TPPL lead-acid and a new lithium battery for data centers, telecom/broadband (DOCSIS 4.0) and utility substations (SEC 8-K 2026-08-12; Investor Day transcript 2026-06-11). Precision Power: defense/aerospace lithium for soldier power, drones and standoff weapons. Industrial Mobility: forklift batteries and Class 8 APUs (Jefferies transcript, aggregator).
web_price_volume_mix: Price-led. Q1 FY27 growth was +3% pricing, +1% FX, +1% organic volume (SEC 8-K 2026-08-12). FY26 was +3% price, +2% FX, +1% acquisitions, -2% organic volume (SEC 8-K 2026-05-20). Mix is favourable: NIS +9.4% and PPS +23.6% offset IMS -3.2%.
web_bottleneck: The company's own bottleneck is the prolonged material-handling recession: IMS sales fell 3.2% y/y in Q1 FY27 (SEC 8-K 2026-08-12). The bottleneck it relieves is customer energy security and labor scarcity (aging grid, too few electricians), plus FEOC-compliant domestic lithium cells because China controls roughly 99% of the LFP supply chain (Investor Day transcript 2026-06-11, aggregator).
web_who_benefits_next: Hyperscalers and UPS OEMs needing reliable data-center backup; the US Department of War and NATO primes; Class 8 truck fleets; warehouse operators via the FORTIX storage system; US utility substations (SEC 8-K 2026-08-12; Investor Day transcript 2026-06-11). Second order: Greenville SC and the DOE-funded domestic supply chain, and EnerSys's own services arm.
web_who_loses: Chinese LFP and lithium cell makers shut out of FEOC-compliant US defense demand; Verkor, which EnerSys intends to drop as technology partner (SEC 8-K 2026-07-23); rival lithium data-center suppliers with slower service; lead-acid-only competitors as EnerSys shifts volume to higher-value maintenance-free and lithium solutions (Investor Day transcript, aggregator).
web_margin_collapse_risk: Loss or phase-out of IRC 45X credits, which added $47.2M, 5.0 points, to Q1 FY27 gross profit and lift GM to 33.5% from 28.5% ex-45X (SEC 8-K 2026-08-12). Also the non-recurring $30.9M tariff refunds, a deeper IMS recession, lithium cell cost inflation, Tijuana closure charges and adverse FX.
web_low_cost_substitute: Yes. Chinese LFP and lithium cells are the cheap substitute and are available commercially now; the CEO says China controls about 99% of the LFP material and supply chain (2026-06-11 Investor Day, aggregator). They are not FEOC-compliant for US defense programs, so EnerSys's domestic alternative only arrives when Greenville, about 1 GWh, starts construction in H1 FY2028 (SEC 8-K 2026-07-23).
web_ceo_promised: At Investor Day on 2026-06-11 CEO Shawn O'Connell and CFO Andi Funk promised a long-term framework: 4-8% annual revenue growth, 3-5% end-market growth and 50-100 bps margin expansion per year, aided by about $875M of remaining buyback (transcript, aggregator). On 2026-08-12 O'Connell pledged a dividend growing with earnings excluding 45X (SEC 8-K).
web_did_they_deliver: Mostly yes. Guidance of $2.95-3.05 Q4 FY26 adj EPS delivered $3.19 (SEC 8-K 2026-05-20); Q1 FY27 guidance of $2.70-2.90 adj EPS on $915-955M sales delivered $3.66 and $935.6M, beating consensus $2.83 (SEC 8-K 2026-08-12). FY26 record sales $3.75B, +4%; $1B cumulative three-year FCF and 150% three-year TSR (Investor Day transcript, aggregator).
web_what_would_falsify: Lithium data-center-backup revenue staying near 0% of NIS by the December earnings call, the prior card's own falsifier. Also: Q2 FY27 (due about early November 2026) adjusted EPS ex-45X below $1.95 or sales below $955M (SEC 8-K 2026-08-12); any curtailment of IRC 45X; or Greenville construction slipping past H1 FY2028 (SEC 8-K 2026-07-23).
